It measures 4-20 mA signals without “breaking the loop,” allowing you to measure low level DC current without having to take systems offline for troubleshooting, saving downtime and money. You can also use it to measure output signals from transmitters without breaking the loop when maintaining and troubleshooting process and automation equipment. This saves time and avoids disrupting critical processes so you can avoid expensive downtime. You can also measure 10 to 50 mA signals in older control systems using the 99.9 mA range.

Designed to make troubleshooting easier, the Fluke 771 includes a detachable clamp that can be attached to the wire you’re testing while you move the meter—connected by the extension cable—to a better viewing position. This is especially helpful for taking readings in tight locations. With the dual backlit display showing both the mA measurement and the percent of a 4 to 20 mA span you can quickly understand what your system is doing, and a built-in LED spotlight lets you illuminate hard to see wire in dark enclosures. You can also capture and display changing measurements using the Hold function making it easier to verify and record measurements

The TJA1021 is the interface between the Local Interconnect Network (LIN) commander/ responder protocol controller and the physical bus in a LIN. It is primarily intended for invehicle sub-networks using baud rates from 1 kBd up to 20 kBd (/20 and B variants) and is compliant with LIN 2.0, LIN 2.1, LIN 2.2, LIN 2.2A, SAE J2602 and ISO 17987-4:2016 (12 V). The TJA1021 is pin-to-pin compatible with the TJA1020 and MC33662(B). The transmit data stream of the protocol controller at the transmit data input (TXD) is converted by the TJA1021 into a bus signal with optimized slew rate and wave shaping to minimize ElectroMagnetic Emission (EME). The LIN bus output pin is pulled HIGH via an internal termination resistor. For a commander application, an external resistor in series with a diode should be connected between pin INH or pin VBAT and pin LIN. The receiver detects the data stream at the LIN bus input pin and transfers it via pin RXD to the microcontroller. In Sleep mode, the power consumption of the TJA1021 is very low. In failure modes, the power consumption is reduced to a minimum.

12V DC 12 Watt UPS V2.0 Power Supply Module Uninterruptible Power Supply Control Board Output 9V Or 12V
Conditions of use for 12W version products:
1. The input external power supply needs sufficient power, and it can ensure that it can drive the load and charge the battery at the same time. Recommended input current is not less than 1.5A
2. The wire diameter of the power input cannot be less than 24AWG, and it needs to withstand a current of 2A or more, and the internal resistance of the wire does not exceed 100 milliohms.
3. The lithium battery is a 3.7V conventional battery with a capacity of not less than 3000 mA, which can be connected in parallel, and the internal resistance of the battery does not exceed 30 mA!

4. The wire diameter of the battery connection cable cannot be thinner than 20AWG, and the current resistance cannot be lower than 6A. It is recommended that the length of the wire is within 10 cm and less than 20 milliohms!
5. The upper limit of the battery capacity cannot exceed the value marked on the back of the motherboard. Once exceeded, the system will disable the charging function and report an error!

6. There is no reverse connection protection for the battery interface. Connecting the wrong polarity will burn the two chips on the right side of the motherboard or cause a short circuit of the battery interface. If the wrong voltage is connected, all chips will be burned!
7. The working voltage of the main board can be set by JP1. When it is not set, the default is input and output = 9V. If short circuit JP1 with solder, the main board works in 12V mode!

8. The charging current of the motherboard can be set using JP2. When not set, the default is slow charging, which can support 3300-6600 mAh batteries. The capacity of the fast charging mode can be doubled!

9. Regarding charging while charging or using after charging, charging while charging mode is equivalent to the uninterruptible power supply function. After being connected, it does not need to be controlled for many years, and it will automatically charge and discharge!
10. The mode of charging before use is similar to the mobile power supply function. It supports input of DC5V-12V power supply to charge the system. Wait for you to get the load before using it!
1. This product cannot be used at full load, because the voltage will drop and the output power will decrease during battery use, so full load will cause the system to shut down in advance!

2. The battery of this product must be independent and cannot be shared with other devices. If it is shared, it may cause the lithium battery protection chip to break down, and you need to add protection components yourself!

3. This product has integrated a lithium battery protection chip, the protection current is 6-10A, the internal resistance is 20 milliohms, if the battery wants to add a protection board, it can not be lower than this data!

4. The main board and the battery need to keep a distance when assembled into a product. The heat of the main board is 30-40 degrees at light load, 60-70 degrees at medium load, and 80-90 degrees at full load!

5. The no-load current of the normal battery interface is 0.2-0.3mA, if it is found to be higher than 0.5mA, it can be judged as a fault such as system leakage or a lithium battery protection chip breakdown!

6. This product is prohibited to be used in brushed motors or inductive loads. If it must be used, please connect a solid capacitor or tantalum capacitor in parallel to the output to filter interference, otherwise it is easy to burn!

7. Pay attention to measuring the voltage of each interface. The input voltage should not be less than 5% of the rated value. For example, if the power supply input 9V requires a voltage of not less than 8.5V when loaded, otherwise it will be abnormal!

8. The input voltage of the product is 5-12V, the withstand voltage of the interface is 16V, and it is easy to break the chip when the input exceeds 16V. Please pay special attention to the voltage value of the input interface, do not overpressure!

9. Regarding the blinking of the indicator light, the charging indicator light displays normally when the battery meets the conditions. If it flashes slowly or quickly, the user needs to check or replace the battery!

10. This product does not support series-connected lithium batteries, but supports parallel-connected batteries, which can be arbitrarily connected in parallel within the capacity range. If the series-connected batteries are mistakenly connected, the main chip will be completely burned!

User tips: JP1 jumper output 12V after short circuit, output 9V when not in operation, battery connection wire can not be lower than 20AWG, it is recommended to use 16-18AWG, on-load start current: 12W version with load start current is 6A, working current is 3A Or lower, and the starting current of the 18W version needs about 10A, and the operating current is 5A or lower. If the wire is too thin, it will cause a voltage drop, which affects performance. Therefore, it is recommended to use thicker leads. Care should be taken to avoid short circuit or polar welding. For wrong and other problems, it is recommended to weld the battery last to prevent the circuit board from being burned out when short circuit or welding error!

The 18W version requires a lower battery limit of 5000 mA, an upper limit of 13,500 mA, and an internal resistance of less than 20 mA. When the battery is below the lower limit, the battery is easily overloaded and causes heat. In severe cases, the battery will catch fire or explode!

About the method of supporting large-capacity batteries: there is a 12-hour CC timer inside the charging chip, and the charging function is automatically disabled when the overcharge is not full. As long as you power off for a few seconds or minutes every 12 hours, you can use the battery in an unlimited amount. Of course, the battery capacity can only be doubled at most. If the capacity is higher, the system may not be able to complete the entire charging process!

blocks.text: Mounted bearings combine a bearing mounted inside a housing unit. The bearing housing replaces the need for a casting or weldment to position the bearing securely for reliable operation, and its design determines the type of insert bearing. Insert bearings use rolling elements (ball, cylindrical, spherical, barrel, needle, spindled, or tapered) to maintain the separation between moving parts to reduce rotational friction, and to support radial and axial loads. Available in a variety of materials and mounting configurations, mounted bearings can be one- or two-piece, they can have an extended inner ring and locking device, and they can have seals and end caps that retain lubrication and protect the working parts of the bearing from environmental debris. Mounted bearings support shafts in a variety of mounting configurations (flange block, hanger, pillow block, and take-up block), and are used in a range of applications from light duty shaft guidance on conveyors to road building equipment and crushers.

makers-341388.summary: Arduino MKR WAN 1310 offers secure, low-power LoRa connectivity featuring a SAMD21 processor and 2MB SPI Flash for advanced IoT applications.

blocks.text: Arduino MKR WAN 1310 LoRa Connectivity (Original Made In Italy)
Arduino MKR WAN 1310 allows you to build your next smart project. Ever wanted an automated house? Or a smart garden?

The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 board provides a practical and cost effective solution to add LoRa® connectivity to projects requiring low power. This open source board can be connected to the Arduino IoT Cloud.
Powered by a Microchip SAMD21 Cortex-M0+ 32-bit ARM processor at 48MHz.
Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa® module supporting 433/868/915 MHz carrier frequencies.
On‑board 2MByte SPI Flash for data logging, over‑the‑air (OTA) updates, and local storage.
ATECC508 cryptographic co‑processor for secure key storage and authentication.
Integrated Li‑Po battery charger with power path management.
Ultra‑low power consumption: as low as 104µA in sleep mode when properly configured.
8 digital I/O pins, 7 analog inputs (8/10/12‑bit ADC), 1 analog output (10‑bit DAC), and 12 PWM channels.
Micro USB port for programming and power (5V input).
Arduino Cloud compatible and supports LoRaWAN® protocols.

The MKR WAN 1310, brings in a series of improvements when compared to its predecessor, the MKR WAN 1300. While still based on the Microchip® SAMD21 low power processor, the Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa® module, and the MKR family’s characteristic crypto chip (the ECC508), the MKR WAN 1310 includes a new battery charger, a 2MByte SPI Flash, and improved control of the board’s power consumption.

The latest modifications have considerably improved the battery life on the MKR WAN 1310. When properly configured, the power consumption is now as low as 104uA! It is also possible to use the USB port to supply power (5V) to the board; run the board with or without batteries – the choice is yours.

Data logging and other OTA (Over The Air) functions are now possible since the inclusion of the on board 2MByte Flash. This new exciting feature will let you transfer configuration files from the infrastructure onto the board, create your own scripting commands, or simply store data locally to send it whenever the connectivity is best. Whilst the MKR WAN 1310’s crypto chip adds further security by storing credentials & certificates in the embedded secure element.
These features make it the perfect IoT node and building block for low-power wide-area IoT devices.

Check the Arduino Forum for questions about the Arduino Language, or how to make your own Projects with Arduino. Need any help with your board please get in touch with the official Arduino User Support as explained in our Contact Us page.
The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 is based on the SAMD21 microcontroller.

Usage Recommendations (Very Important) | توصيات الاستخدام (مهم جدًا)
🧼 Cleanliness first: Ensure PCB surfaces and components are clean and free of dust or residues.
🧴 Apply appropriately: Coat the PCB and components with flux using a suitable method (dip, wave, spray, or mist).

Dip Soldering: Fix the PCB with a holder or crucible plier tong, then immerse in molten solder using the proper machine technique for 3–10 seconds; a slight motion (optional) helps cover all points evenly.
Wave Soldering: Preheat the PCB to activate the flux and protect from thermal shock, then move the PCB across the molten solder waves.
❄️ Cooling: Allow the PCB to cool in air until the solder solidifies.
🧽 Cleaning (optional): If needed, remove residues with alcohol or thinner.
🧼 النظافة أولًا: تأكّد من خلو سطح اللوحة ومكوّناتها من الغبار وبقايا الشحوم.

blocks.text: This screw-terminal aluminum electrolytic capacitor rated at 2200 µF and 250 V is a high-capacitance, high-voltage component designed for power smoothing and energy-buffering tasks. Its construction uses an aluminum can, a wound aluminum foil dielectric and a liquid electrolyte, with large terminals (screw posts) for secure, low-impedance connections. This form factor is chosen when large bulk capacitance and robust mounting are required.

In service, the device acts as an energy reservoir: when voltage is applied, charge accumulates across the dielectric, allowing rapid delivery or absorption of current spikes and smoothing of voltage fluctuations. The screw-terminal design helps minimize series resistance and inductance, making it suitable for use in circuits with significant current and switching demands. Its 250 V rating gives adequate headroom for many DC link or intermediate bus applications.

Mechanically the unit is larger than typical electrolyte types because of the high voltage and capacitance rating. The screw terminals facilitate heavy-duty connections, often using lugs or tabs rather than simple PCB links. Because it uses aluminum foil and liquid electrolyte, lifespan is influenced by temperature, ripple current and environmental stress. Proper mounting, ventilation and derating contribute to its reliable long-term use in industrial or power-electronic settings.

The 2N6124 is a silicon PNP power transistor in a through-hole TO-220 package, engineered to serve as a rugged switching and amplification device in power electronics. Its design emphasises robust handling of collector-emitter stresses and reliable electrical behavior under repetitive switching conditions. The device’s mechanical format (TO-220) enables easy mounting and effective heat sinking for sustained power operation.

Electrically, the transistor is intended to deliver controlled, predictable PNP switching performance across a range of drive conditions. The datasheet frames the device for use where stable gain and repeatable saturation characteristics are required, noting that drive margins and saturation behavior have been optimized to support both continuous and pulsed loads. Thermal design guidance and ratings are provided to help ensure that the transistor maintains performance when subjected to high dissipation and temperature stresses.

Emphasis in the datasheet is placed on manufacturing consistency and long-term reliability, making the 2N6124 suitable for demanding power amplifier and switching roles in consumer and industrial equipment. The combination of a robust semiconductor process, conservative thermal limits, and a common through-hole package helps designers integrate the part into systems that require straightforward mounting, maintainable cooling, and predictable service life.

The HCF4511BE is a compact CMOS BCD-to-7-segment latch/decoder/driver offered in a 16-pin DIP (and SOIC) package. It accepts a 4-bit BCD input and converts it into the seven segment outputs required to drive a single 7-segment LED display, combining CMOS logic for low quiescent current with bipolar output stages that can source display current directly. The device integrates input latches so codes can be stored and displayed independently of changing input lines.

The IC includes auxiliary control pins such as lamp test and blanking, enabling easy diagnostic testing of the display and blanking of segments when required. It also provides standardized, symmetrical output characteristics and balanced propagation delays to keep segment transitions even and predictable. Because the outputs are designed to source current, the HCF4511BE is especially suitable for driving common-anode style LED segments when used according to the datasheet’s wiring recommendations.

Overall, the HCF4511BE simplifies numeric display designs by removing the need for discrete decoder logic and separate driver transistors. Its latch capability and built-in test/blanking functions reduce external components and wiring, making it a convenient choice for counters, meters, consumer electronics readouts and similar single-digit numeric display applications.

makers-325427.summary: 1000μF 16V capacitor stores and filters energy in electronic circuits, ideal for power supplies, audio systems, and voltage stabilization.

blocks.text: The 1000μF 16V capacitor is a commonly used electrolytic capacitor designed for energy storage, filtering, and voltage regulation in a wide range of electronic circuits. With a capacitance of 1000 microfarads (μF) and a voltage rating of 16 volts, this component is ideal for low to moderate voltage applications such as power supplies, amplifiers, LED drivers, and microcontroller systems.

As an aluminum electrolytic capacitor, it provides high capacitance in a compact size, making it suitable for circuits that require bulk energy storage or smoothing of DC voltage. It works by charging and discharging energy to compensate for voltage drops or spikes, improving the stability of the overall system. This function is especially critical in power regulation, where it helps maintain a steady voltage level by reducing ripple.

The 1000μF 16V capacitor is polarized, meaning it has positive and negative terminals and must be installed with the correct orientation. Incorrect polarity can lead to malfunction or damage. Please use an external switching power supply, and the voltage as close as possible to the +5.00V. More accurate the voltage, the higher the accuracy!

The ADC0808 IC is a commonly used ADC module for projects were an external ADC is required. It is a 28-pin Eight channel 8-bit ADC module. Meaning it can measure up to eight ADC value from 0V to 5V and the precision when voltage reference (Vref –pin 9) is +5V is 19.53mV (Step size). That is for every increase of 19.53mV on input side there will be an increase of 1 bit at the output side.

This IC is very Ideal to use with Microprocessors like Raspberry Pi, Beagle bone etc.. Or even to use as a standalone ADC module. Every ADC module requires a clock to function; this IC requires an external clock pulse to work. Hence, if you are looking for a ADC module with a decent resolution of 8-bit that could measure up to 8 channels then this IC is for you.

Since the ADC0808 IC can measure up to eight Analog voltage and also does not have an internal clock slightly requires more components to make it work compared to its predecessor ADC0804. The IC can be powered by +5V. The Vref + and the Output enable should also be supplied +5V to obtained the output. Powering the V ref + with +5V will make the IC operate with a step size of 19.53mV. The external clock should be connected to clock pin, this can either be a oscillator circuit or can just be an pulse generated from a MCU/MPU.

The right input analog voltage can be given to pins from IN1 to IN7, but the IC can read the voltage of only one channel at a time. 2N3906 is a PNP transistor hence the collector and emitter will be closed (Forward biased) when the base pin is held at ground and will be opened (Reverse biased) when a signal is provided to base pin. This is where a PNP transistor differs from a NPN transistor, a Logic state (blue colour) is used to toggle between Ground and Signal Voltage (Emitter-Base Voltage VBE) as shown below

2N3906 has a gain value of 110 to 300, this value determines the amplification capacity of the transistor. The maximum amount of current that could flow through the Collector pin is 200mA, hence we cannot connect loads that consume more than 200mA using this transistor. To bias a transistor we have to supply current to base pin, this current (IB) should be limited to 5mA.

When this transistor is fully biased then it can allow a maximum of 200mA to flow across the collector and emitter. This stage is called Saturation Region and the typical voltage allowed across the Collector-Emitter (V­CE) or Base-Emitter (VBE) could be 40 and 5 V respectively. When base current is removed the transistor becomes fully off, this stage is called as the Cut-off Region and the Base Emitter voltage could be around 5V.

The 2N3906 is a commonly used PNP transistor. It very much similar to the bc557 transistor except for that it has high collector to emitter voltage and hence high voltage loads can be toggled. This transistor has only a gain value of 300, hence not suitable for amplifier circuits.

The General Purpose Relay SPDT (1 Form C) 6VDC Coil 10A Through Hole 5 Pin is a highly versatile and reliable electromechanical switch designed to meet the demands of various electronic applications. Relays are critical components in electronics, enabling low-power control signals to manage high-power circuits effectively. This relay features a Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) configuration, also known as 1 Form C, which includes both normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC) contacts. This configuration allows the relay to switch a single input between two outputs, providing flexibility for diverse control scenarios in automation, automotive, and industrial systems.
Provides electrical isolation between coil and contacts.
Normally open and normally closed switching paths.

Normally Open (NO) · The other end of the load is either connected to NO or NC. If connected to NO the load remains disconnected before trigger

This module is a DC adjustable constant voltage constant current step down power supply module with LCD display. HD display input voltage and output voltage, current, power and display status. Soft Starter: Yes(Failure at high power load)
Long press means need keep press for more than 3 second.
ON/OFF: Short Press to select whether output. Long press is used to restore default settings.
IN/OUT: Short Press to switch display input voltage or output voltage. Long press is used to switch display output current or output power.
CV Potentiometer: Adjust output voltage. Increase the output voltage when rotating clockwise.
CC Potentiometer: Adjust output current. Increase the output current when rotating clockwise.
OUT LED: Green LED, Output indicator. It will turn ON when there is a output at output terminal.
CC LED: Red LED, Constant current output indicator. It enters the constant current state when the load current reaches the set current and CC constant current indicator turns ON.
As an ordinary step down power module:
Connect right input voltage at input terminal.
Adjust CV constant voltage potentiometer to set output voltage according to require.
Rotate CC potentiometer counterclockwise more than 10 turns at first.
Test Output short circuit current by multimeter at 10A or 20A(Connect two Test Probes to output terminal on module)
Rotate CC constant current potentiometer clockwise to set output current according to require overcurrent protection value.
Test and using(e.g: Module’s maximum output current is 2A if display 2A on multimeter. Red LED indicator will turn on if output reach to 2A. Otherwise LED is OFF.)

Tops: Power module can’t be used as charger module if it does not support constant current function. The voltage difference between the battery with insufficient voltage and the charger is very large. Causes excessive charging current even damage the battery. So it need keep charging in constant current mode to reaching a certain level. Then automatically switch back to constant voltage charging.

Make sure floating charge voltage and charge current for battery. If the lithium battery’s parameter is 3.7V/2200mAh, then the float charge voltage is 4.2V, and the maximum charging current is 1C, which is 2200mA. Connect right input voltage at input terminal.(Note: Please don’t connect load during set parameter) Test output voltage by multimeter and adjust CC potentiometer to make sure output voltage reach to require floating charge voltage. (If charge a 3.7V lithium battery, adjust the output voltage to 4.2V) Rotate CC potentiometer counterclockwise more than 10 turns at first.
Test Output short circuit current by multimeter at 10A or 20A(Connect two Test Probes to output terminal on module)
Rotate CC constant current potentiometer clockwise to set output current according to require charge current value.
Connect battery at output terminal and start to charge.
As a high power LED constant current driver:
Make sure LED working current and maximum working voltage.
Connect right input voltage at input terminal.(Note: Please don’t connect load during set parameter).
Test output voltage by multimeter at output terminal and adjust CV potentiometer to set output voltage to LED’s maximum working voltage.
Rotate CC potentiometer counterclockwise more than 10 turns.
Test Output short circuit current by multimeter at 10A or 20A(Connect two Test Probes to output terminal on module)
Rotate CC constant current potentiometer clockwise to set output current according to require LED working current.
Default output voltage and current is about 18V 7A.
It is a step down power supply module, so the output voltage must be lower than input voltage. Otherwise it will not working normally.
Please rotate the CV potentiometer counterclockwise more than 20 turns if there is no output voltage. It is a DC power module, so it can’t connect to AC power.

Please don’t short output because 7A by default. Please set down output voltage less than 10V and rotate CC potentiometer counterclockwise more than 10 turns. And then short output to adjust output current. Input voltage must be 0.8V higher than output voltage.

Please connect input before connect battery when use as charge and make sure output voltage is higher than battery voltage. It is recommended to serial an anti-backflow diode at input positive terminal.
“IN-” and “OUT-” can’t be connect together, otherwise module can’t support constant current output.
Please make sure input power is more than load power.
Please step down output power if module is hot.

ومن أهم مميزات هذا المنتج أنه مصمم للتثبيت على اللوحة، لذلك فهو مناسب جدًا للوحات التحكم، وصناديق الكهرباء، وأنظمة الإضاءة، ووحدات التوزيع، والتوصيلات داخل الأجهزة والمعدات المختلفة. هذا النوع من التثبيت يساهم في تحسين شكل التوصيلات، وزيادة ثباتها، وتنظيم مسار الأسلاك داخل النظام بشكل أفضل.

blocks.text: 220V to 9V AC and 18V-0-18V AC 2A Dual Output Center-Tapped Step-Down Transformer

This 2A step-down power transformer converts a 220V AC mains input into two separate low-voltage AC outputs. The secondary side provides one 0-9V AC output through two wires and one center-tapped 18V-0-18V AC output through three wires, giving a total of five secondary output wires.

The separate secondary windings make this transformer suitable for projects that require a dedicated 9V AC supply together with a higher-voltage symmetrical 18V-0-18V AC supply. After adding suitable rectifier, filtering, and voltage-regulation circuits, the outputs can be used to build single-rail or positive and negative DC power supplies for amplifiers, control systems, and other electronic circuits.

blocks.text: Type-C USB 3S BMS 15W 12.6V Lithium Battery Charging Boost Module with Balanced Support

a compact, high‑efficiency lithium battery charging and boost module purpose‑built for three‑cell (3S) 18650/Li‑ion packs. It brings modern USB‑C convenience to makers, repair technicians, and product engineers who need a fast, tidy way to charge 11.1–12.6 V battery packs from any Type‑C power adapter—while keeping safety, configurability, and reliability front and center.

✅ USB‑C input with fast‑charge negotiation — Plug into a USB‑C wall charger or power bank and the module automatically aligns to the supported fast‑charge profile to maximize the available power budget. This lets the board deliver up to 15 W to the battery pack without bulky brick supplies.

⚙️ Native 3S charging — Out of the box the default configuration supports two cells, and a simple pad short enables 3S mode (12.6 V full‑charge) for three series cells. The layout clearly labels the configuration pads and balance/BM connection so you can adapt the board to your pack architecture in minutes.

🔋 Up to 1.5 A charge current — The current set network gives you practical control of charge current to match cell capacity and thermal limits. Use the onboard resistor options or replace with your value; the reference formula (I ≈ 90 000 / Rset) makes sizing straightforward for 0.3–1.5 A ranges.

🔌 Synchronous boost‑charging core — A high‑efficiency switching architecture converts USB input power into regulated multi‑cell charging with minimal heat rise, achieving efficiency up to ~94% under typical conditions. Less wasted heat means better stability inside compact enclosures.

🛡️ Smart protections — Built‑in logic supervises input undervoltage, thermal behavior, timeout options, and fault indication. Clear LED states (red power, blue charging/full, blue flashing abnormal) keep status visible during bring‑up and service.

🧩 Balanced system awareness — The board includes a BM sense pin for inter‑cell connection when used with two cells, supporting equalization behavior in 2S mode. In 3S mode you should pair the charger with a proper 3S protection/BMS board to provide pack‑level protections and cell health management.
🧱 Tiny footprint — At roughly 32 × 18 × 5 mm, the module drops into tight projects: handheld tools, LED rigs, IoT nodes, portable speakers, and robotics where every cubic millimeter counts.

🌡️ Optional NTC input — For applications that require temperature‑aware charging, the board exposes an NTC header. Fit the recommended thermistor and value network to enable temperature gating during charge cycles.
✅ True USB‑C convenience: No barrel jacks. No custom adapters. A single reversible connector and broad compatibility with USB‑C power bricks makes field charging simpler and more user‑friendly.

🚀 15 W class performance: For typical 3S packs in the 1500–4000 mAh range, a 1–1.5 A charge current hits a practical sweet spot for turnaround time without stressing cells—ideal for daily‑use prototyping and small‑batch products.

🧠 Engineer‑friendly configurability: The configuration pads, current‑set resistors, VSET network for termination voltage, optional charge timeout programming, and BM/NTC breakouts give you the right knobs to tune behavior to your cells and enclosure.
🪛 Service‑ready indicators: The two‑color LED scheme dramatically speeds fault isolation on the bench. Power presence, charging, charge‑complete, and abnormal conditions are obvious at a glance.

🛠️ Robust to mixed input sources: Whether you feed via Type‑C with a QC/fast‑charge adapter or via the solder pads from a DC rail, the module handles real‑world input variance gracefully. When input is below pack voltage, it enters boost state and continues charging appropriately.
🔌 3S 18650 battery packs powering compact amplifiers, FPV gear, lab tools, or custom handhelds.
💡 LED light bars and cine rigs where 12 V rails are common and fast recharge is critical between shoots.
📡 IoT gateways and edge controllers that must stay untethered and hot‑swappable during maintenance windows.
🎛️ Portable test instruments—multimeters, logic probes, and fixtures—upgraded from 2S to 3S packs for higher headroom.
🤖 Robotics subsystems like gimbal drivers or small actuators that prefer a stable 12 V bus.

Input: USB Type‑C port or solder‑pad input. Compatible with common fast‑charge profiles for elevated input voltage/current. 5 V sources supported; fast‑charge negotiation improves delivered power headroom.
Battery: 3S Li‑ion/Li‑polymer (nominal 11.1 V, 12.6 V full). Default board ships in 2S; set configuration pads to enable 3S.
Max charge current: Up to 1.5 A (programmable). Reference: I (A) ≈ 90 000 / Rset (kΩ) using the current‑set network. Example: 100 kΩ ≈ 0.9 A; 180 kΩ ≈ 0.5 A.
Termination voltage: 4.2 V per cell (adjustable via VSET network if your chemistry requires).
Timeout (optional): 4 h at 68 kΩ, 12 h at 120 kΩ, 24 h default (no resistor).
Temperature sense (optional): Fit 100 kΩ NTC (B≈4100) with recommended network; change on‑board fixed resistor to ~82 kΩ.
Indicators: Red = power; Blue = charging; Blue off = full; Blue flashing = abnormal.

Note on balancing: Equalization behavior is supported in 2S wiring via BM connection. For 3S builds, use an external 3S BMS/protection board for cell balancing, over/under‑voltage, and pack protections.
🔧 1) Configure for 3S: Short the 3S configuration pads as indicated on the PCB silkscreen, and remove the side resistor per the standard procedure. Verify continuity and clean flux residues.

🪫 2) Wire the pack: Connect B‑ to pack negative, BM to the mid‑point between cell 2 and 3 if specified by your BMS (for 2S balance only; in 3S use BM according to your protection board’s guidance), and B+ to pack positive.

🔌 3) Provide input: Use a 15–20 W USB‑C charger for best results. Alternatively, feed the solder pads with a clean DC source within the supported range. If the input is below pack voltage the module will operate in boost mode.

Nominal voltage: 11.1 V (3.7 V per cell)
Charge voltage (full): 12.6 V (4.2 V per cell)

Balance: JST-XH 4-pin (3S). Always balance-charge to maintain cell health.
Lead length: compact pigtails to reduce resistive loss; avoid extensions where possible.

blocks.text: IC 74139 – Dual 2-to-4 Line Decoder / Demultiplexer (74HC139 / 74LS139, DIP-16)

The IC 74139 is a dual 2-to-4 line decoder and demultiplexer with active-LOW outputs and independent enable inputs for each section. Each half of the chip decodes 2 binary inputs into 4 mutually exclusive outputs. Available in 74HC139 (CMOS) and 74LS139 (TTL) families, this IC is widely used for chip-select logic, memory addressing, and control signal routing.
Fast decoding and short propagation delay.
DIP-16 package suitable for breadboard and prototyping.
Only one output is LOW at a time (one-hot).

This Arduino Uno is an original microcontroller board from Arduino officials based on the ATmega328P. blocks.text: The 74138 is a high-speed 3-to-8 line decoder/demultiplexer in a 16-pin DIP package. A 3-bit binary code on its address inputs A, B and C selects one of eight outputs, which goes LOW while the other seven stay HIGH. Three enable inputs make it easy to cascade chips into larger decoders, which is why the 74138 is a standard part for memory and I/O address decoding, chip-select logic and expanding microcontroller outputs.
Enables: G1 active HIGH; G2A and G2B active LOW
Pins 1, 2, 3: A, B, C (address inputs, A = least significant bit)
Pins 15 to 9: Y0 to Y6, Pin 7: Y7

Connect G1 to 5V, G2A and G2B to GND, and A, B, C to Arduino pins 2, 3 and 4. For an indicator, connect an LED cathode to an output and its anode through 1KΩ to 5V: (5V − 2V − 0.4V) ÷ 1KΩ ≈ 2.6 mA. This function selects output n (0 to 7):
void selectOutput(int n) { digitalWrite(2, n & 1); digitalWrite(3, (n >> 1) & 1); digitalWrite(4, (n >> 2) & 1); }
Chip-select lines for several SPI devices
If no output goes LOW, check the enables: G1 must be HIGH and both G2A and G2B must be LOW.

2.2µF capacitor between Input and Ground, close to the regulator.
With electrolytic capacitors, connect the positive lead to Ground, because the input and output are negative.
The regulator turns the extra voltage into heat: P = (|Vin| − 5V) × I. For example, a −12V input at 0.3A gives (12 − 5) × 0.3 = 2.1W, which needs a heatsink.

blocks.text: The RAMPS 1.4 Control Board (RepRap Arduino Mega Pololu Shield) is one of the most widely used controller boards for DIY 3D printers, CNC machines, and laser engravers. Designed to work with the Arduino Mega 2560, it provides a modular and expandable platform for controlling stepper motors, heaters, fans, thermistors, and endstops.

The board supports up to five StepStick-compatible stepper driver modules, including A4988, DRV8825, TMC2100, TMC2208, TMC2209, and other compatible drivers. Its modular design allows drivers to be easily replaced or upgraded as needed.

RAMPS 1.4 features dedicated outputs for the heated bed, hotend, and cooling fan, along with three thermistor inputs for accurate temperature monitoring. It also includes expansion headers for LCD displays, servos, I2C, SPI, and endstops, making it an excellent choice for custom 3D printer builds and upgrades.

blocks.text: The CD4028 is a CMOS BCD-to-decimal decoder IC designed to convert binary-coded decimal (BCD) input into a one-of-ten decimal output. It takes a 4-bit BCD input (0000 to 1001) and activates the corresponding one of ten outputs (0–9), with all other outputs remaining LOW. For input codes 1010 to 1111, all outputs remain LOW, ensuring valid BCD decoding only.
This decoder is ideal for numeric display control, digital instrumentation, and other applications where binary-to-decimal conversion is needed.
